sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Component-modeled vintage three-head tape echo with a three-spring reverb tank. Port of Tape Echo 2 by Dusk Audio (GPL-3.0). The record EQ and tape saturation sit INSIDE the feedback loop, so each repeat darkens and compresses instead of just getting quieter — which is what lets high Intensity settings bloom into warm, stable self-oscillation.  Three pages: MAIN is eight controls that cover what you normally reach for, ADVANCED is the tape path itself, OUT is the wet levels. Nothing is hidden — every parameter is still on a page.

sections.heading: Main: the eight
sections.body: TIME sets the delay in milliseconds. SYNC locks it to the project tempo. FBK is feedback — how many repeats. MIX is dry against wet. TONE, WIDTH and TAPE are macros: one knob each over several of the engine's controls, so the front page reaches the whole machine without you going looking. MODE picks which playback heads are live.

sections.heading: TIME (and why it never fights MODE)
sections.body: Shown in milliseconds, not as a 0..1 rate. The reachable span depends on which head MODE has selected — head 1 covers about 69-177 ms, head 3 about 191-490 ms — so TIME works within the current head and pins at the motor limit rather than silently switching heads underneath you. With SYNC on it picks a tempo division instead, so it is never a dead knob.

sections.heading: TONE (macro)
sections.body: A tilt, not a filter sweep. Right of centre lifts the treble and eases the bass; left does the reverse; centre is flat. It drives the BASS and TREBLE shelves on the ADVANCED page, which you can still set individually.

sections.heading: TAPE (macro)
sections.body: How worn the machine is. It drives W&F and AGE together, which belong together: the tape's age multiplies its wow and flutter, roughly 1x / 1.8x / 3.4x across New, Used and Old. It deliberately does NOT touch DRIVE — that is a level control, a different question.

sections.heading: WIDTH (macro)
sections.body: How far successive repeats swing left and right. Raising it from zero switches PONG on for you, because width does nothing on its own. Turning PONG off by hand afterwards sticks — WIDTH will not switch it back.

sections.heading: MODE
sections.body: Which of the three playback heads are live, and whether the spring tank is in circuit. Digits are the heads, R is reverb: H1, H2, H3, H2+3, H1+R, H2+R, H3+R, H12+R, H23+R, H13+R, H123R, Rev. Head 1 is the shortest tap, head 3 the longest (about 1.00 / 1.91 / 2.76 times the motor time). Rev is spring only, no tape.

sections.heading: FBK (Intensity)
sections.body: Feedback — how much of the playback head sum is fed back onto the tape. Above roughly three quarters it self-oscillates and builds into a growing drone. That is the hardware behaviour, and it gets loud: ride Echo Volume.

sections.heading: Mix
sections.body: Dry against the combined wet bus. 50 percent is the classic parallel setting with both paths at unity — below that the dry stays at unity while the wet fades in, above it the wet stays at unity while the dry fades out. 0 is fully dry, 100 fully wet.

sections.heading: SYNC
sections.body: Locks the leading active head to the host tempo instead of the Repeat Rate knob. The note comes from the Echo Rate Note detent, read through whichever head is leading in the current Mode.

sections.heading: Advanced: the tape path
sections.body: In signal order. ARM is whether anything is being recorded onto the tape. DRIVE is how hard. AGE and W&F are the condition of the tape. BASS and TREBLE are the echo path's EQ, inside the feedback loop, which is why every repeat darkens a little more than the last.

sections.heading: ARM
sections.body: Whether the input is being recorded onto the tape. Off, you still hear yourself dry and the repeats already on the tape keep playing and fading — the dub throw. New sound stops going on, existing sound is untouched. Note it gates the TAPE only: in a mode with R, the spring reverb still receives what you play, so you stay audible in the reverb with the echo held.

sections.heading: DRIVE
sections.body: Preamp gain into the record stage. Higher settings push the tape into saturation and soft compression before anything is recorded, thickening the repeats.

sections.heading: AGE
sections.body: Cartridge condition. New is a fresh tape and serviced transport. Used and Old progressively add noise, more wow, high-frequency loss, level wobble and splice wear.

sections.heading: W&F
sections.body: Transport instability: slow wow, capstan flutter, and a stochastic scrape band around 6 Hz. Zero is not perfectly still — the modeled transport always has some motion, matching the reference machine.  One control over three kinds of motion: wow at about 0.5 Hz, flutter up to about 3.9 Hz, and a stochastic 6-100 Hz scrape band. AGE scales all of it.

sections.heading: BASS
sections.body: Low shelf on the echo path only, about plus or minus 17 dB. The dry signal is untouched. Cutting bass keeps long feedback washes from turning muddy.

sections.heading: TREBLE
sections.body: High shelf on the echo path only, about plus or minus 17 dB. Because it is inside the loop, cutting treble makes each successive repeat darker than the last.

sections.heading: Out
sections.body: ECHO and VERB are the two wet levels, under MIX. PONG and DIV are the raw halves of MAIN's WIDTH and SYNC, here for when you want them directly. The reverb comes up at a usable level so that choosing a +R mode is audible straight away.

sections.heading: ECHO
sections.body: Level of the tape echo path in the output mix. Independent of Reverb Volume, so you can run either alone.

sections.heading: VERB
sections.body: Level of the spring tank. Only audible in the modes that include R. The tank is three bidirectional dispersive springs, so an impulse arrives as an ascending chirp and each round trip gets darker and more smeared.

sections.heading: PONG
sections.body: Sends successive repeats to alternate sides. Each playback head runs its own alternation at its own delay, so the multi-head modes separate properly instead of smearing. The tape loop itself is untouched: one mono tape, the same repeat train and the same tape character as always — only the side each repeat leaves from changes. With Ping Pong off the echo is the centred mono bus it has always been.

sections.heading: DIV
sections.body: The eleven physical tempo-sync detents, 1 (longest) to 11 (shortest). The same detent means a different note depending on the leading head, exactly as on the hardware — changing Mode keeps the detent and reassigns its note. Notes the transport cannot physically reach are pinned at the motor limit rather than transposed.

sections.heading: WIDTH (raw)
sections.body: How far Ping Pong swings, from centred at 0 to hard left and right at 100. Constant power across the sweep, so widening never changes the level. Only does anything while Ping Pong is on. A TapeDelay patch's stereo width arrives here and switches Ping Pong on, since width is what made that module's two cross-fed delay lines alternate.

sections.heading: TapeDelay presets
sections.body: Tape Echo 2 reads settings saved by the older TapeDelay module (schwung-space-delay). A patch names the module it wants, so run tools/convert_tapedelay_patch.py on it first to point that slot here; the settings themselves are then translated on load. Its delay time picks the playback head that can actually reach it — head 1 covers about 69 to 177 ms, head 2 up to 339, head 3 up to 490 — and the motor is set from there; times outside that range pin at the nearest end. Feedback scales to just under self-oscillation, mix and tone carry across (tone becomes the treble shelf), and a note division switches tempo sync on at the nearest detent. Stereo width maps to the Ping Pong widener and switches it on.  A fresh insert lands there too: the defaults are what an untouched TapeDelay becomes through that same import, so it opens as a 400 ms echo rather than as this engine's own slapback.

sections.heading: Credits
sections.body: DSP: Tape Echo 2 by Dusk Audio, github.com/dusk-audio/dusk-audio-plugins, GPL-3.0. The core carries one Schwung-specific change, marked in the files: a per-head Ping Pong stage on the echo output tap. With Ping Pong off it is the original sample for sample, and the build checks that against a fresh copy of upstream. Move port by athousanddetails.
